about: The first prayer closely follows Daniel 3:39–40. The Mass reverses the order of “in ánimo contríto” and “in spíritu humilitátis” while retaining the plural “suscipiámur” — “may we be received”. The second prayer begins with “Veni” — “come” — addressed to the Sanctifier.

s01.narrative: The priest makes the sign of the cross with the chalice, sets it on the corporal and covers it with the pall. Then, bowed slightly with hands joined upon the altar, the priest says the prayer.

narrative_citations.title: Missale Romanum (1962)
narrative_citations.locator: Ordo Missae rubric before In spiritu humilitatis

s02.translation: With humble spirit and contrite heart may we be accepted by You, O Lord, and may our sacrifice in Your sight this day be pleasing to You, Lord God.

s03.narrative: The priest stands upright, extends his hands, raises and joins them, lifting his eyes to heaven and at once lowering them.

narrative_citations.title: Missale Romanum (1962)
narrative_citations.locator: Ordo Missae rubric before Veni sanctificator

s05.narrative: The priest blesses the offerings and continues the prayer.

narrative_citations.title: Missale Romanum (1962)
narrative_citations.locator: Ordo Missae rubric within Veni sanctificator

s06.translation: and bless this sacrifice, prepared for Your holy name.

w003.function: Genitive depending on “spíritu” (w002): a spirit of humility.

w008.function: First person plural passive. The petition concerns our being received.

w027.function: Singular vocative, identical in form to the nominative.
